pages.title: SHIFT: how youth workers explored AI, IoT and gamified learning in Lithuania

blocks.heading: SHIFT: how youth workers explored AI, IoT and gamified learning in Lithuania
blocks.body:
From 15 to 22 October 2026, Inovatyvi karta (Innovative Generation) hosted the international training course SHIFT – Smart Hands-on Innovation & Facilitation Tech in Youth Work. The course took place near Trakai, Lithuania. It brought together 29 youth workers, youth leaders, project managers and educators from 13 countries who work with young people every day: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bulgaria, Georgia, Hungary, Lithuania, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Türkiye and Ukraine.

The aim of SHIFT was to give youth workers practical knowledge, digital tools and ethical frameworks. With these, they can bring Artificial Intelligence, the Internet of Things (IoT) and gamified learning into modern youth work. The focus was on trying, not on heavy theory.

blocks.heading: From AI basics to AI agents
blocks.body: After the first day of team building, the group looked at the past, present and future of Artificial Intelligence. Participants tested AI tools, explored how AI can support youth exchanges and other youth projects, and experimented with AI agents and AI-powered spaces.

blocks.heading: IoT and gamified learning, hands-on
blocks.body: The IoT days turned the training room into a lab. Smart locks, QR codes, ropes and puzzles became an escape-room style challenge. Participants solved it in teams and then took it apart to see how it was built. The next day was dedicated to gamified learning: how game elements can raise motivation and teamwork in non-formal education.

blocks.heading: Ethics, safety and well-being
blocks.body: Innovation needs responsibility. A session on AI and cybersecurity and open debates on ethical dilemmas pushed the group to reflect. One question was whether youth workers should report a young person who tracks an ex-partner's phone. Data protection and safe technology use were part of the whole programme. So was well-being: daily well-being time, movement and offline moments helped the group keep a healthy balance with screens.

blocks.heading: Learning from local practice
blocks.body: On day four the group visited Trakai Youth Center. A local youth worker shared how youth work operates in Lithuania and what her daily work looks like. The afternoon continued with well-being time in Trakai.

blocks.heading: From ideas to action
blocks.body:
In the last days participants chose tools, worked in production teams and showcased their creations. They then planned follow-up and dissemination activities for their organisations and local communities. Evenings were filled with reflection groups, socialising and intercultural nights.

The learning does not stop here. Participants will meet again online for an evaluation call on 10 December 2026 to share how they have used SHIFT in their work.

We thank all participants, our trainers Gvantsa Mezvrishvili and Vytautas Šliuburys, project manager Artūrs Paparde, and our partners for supporting participants.

Co-funded by the European Union. Views and opinions expressed are however those of the author(s) only and do not necessarily reflect those of the European Union or the Youth Affairs Agency. Neither the European Union nor the granting authority can be held responsible for them.

English — Building confidence and connections in construction: CoHER local meet-up in Budapest
blocks.body:
5 October 2026 — CoHER / KIA Budapest Local Meet-up

On 5 October 2026, Kreatív Ifjúsági Akadémia Magyarország (KIA) brought together 22 participants at Arena in Budapest for a CoHER local meet-up focused on support networks, practical workplace skills and women’s participation in construction.

The group included ten female students in construction-related vocational education, three educators and an industry representative. Twelve attendees were women.

Facilitated by Heemanshu Gupta, the event gave participants space to discuss the challenges women face in construction and explore solutions together. Using Module B scenario cards, groups roleplayed situations involving workplace communication and safety, then discussed possible responses.

Participants also explored the CoHER platform and educational materials. They particularly valued the practical exercises and direct conversations with educators and the industry representative. Suggestions for future events included more time for the exercises and involving more industry representatives.

“It was very useful to see the challenges other girls face in the construction industry, and it was good to find solutions together.”

“It was very useful to discuss practical situations with the industry expert and the teachers. I feel much more confident about my future career in construction.”

Both quotations are translated from Hungarian.

Participants received certificates, and the event concluded with informal networking.

The meet-up contributed to CoHER’s support-network, soft-skills and feedback activities.

Learn more about ConstructHer Future: https://constructherfuture.eu/

Co-funded by the European Union.
Project number: 2024-1-IE01-KA220-VET-000257661

#CoHER #ConstructHerFuture #ErasmusPlus #WomenInConstruction #VocationalEducation #KIA

Magyar — Kapcsolatok és önbizalom az építőiparban – CoHER-találkozó Budapesten
blocks.body:
2026. október 5. — CoHER / KIA Budapest Local Meet-up

2026. október 5-én a Kreatív Ifjúsági Akadémia Magyarország (KIA) 22 résztvevővel rendezett helyi CoHER-találkozót a budapesti Arénában. A program középpontjában a támogató kapcsolatok kialakítása, a munkahelyi készségek gyakorlása és a nők építőipari részvétele állt.

A résztvevők között tíz, építőiparhoz kapcsolódó szakképzésben tanuló lány, három oktató és egy iparági képviselő is jelen volt. Összesen tizenkét nő vett részt az eseményen.

A Heemanshu Gupta által vezetett programon a résztvevők megvitatták az építőiparban dolgozó vagy oda készülő nők előtt álló kihívásokat, és közösen kerestek megoldásokat. A B modul szituációs kártyáival munkahelyi kommunikációs és biztonsági helyzeteket játszottak el, majd megbeszélték a lehetséges válaszokat.

A résztvevők a CoHER online platformjával és tananyagaival is megismerkedtek. Különösen értékesnek tartották az életszerű gyakorlatokat, valamint az oktatókkal és az iparági képviselővel folytatott közvetlen beszélgetéseket. A következő alkalmakra több időt javasoltak a gyakorlati feladatokra, és szívesen találkoznának több iparági szakemberrel.

“Nagyon hasznos volt látni, hogy más lányok milyen kihívásokkal szembesülnek az építőiparban, és jó volt közösen megoldásokat találni.”

“Nagyon hasznos volt a gyakorlati helyzetek átbeszélése az iparági szakértővel és a tanárokkal. Sokkal magabiztosabbnak érzem magam a jövőbeli építőipari karrieremmel kapcsolatban.”

A résztvevők részvételi igazolást kaptak, a programot pedig kötetlen beszélgetés és kapcsolatépítés zárta.

A találkozó a CoHER projekt támogató hálózatépítési, készségfejlesztési és értékelési tevékenységeihez kapcsolódott.

További információ a ConstructHer Future projektről: https://constructherfuture.eu/

Az Európai Unió társfinanszírozásával.
Projektazonosító: 2024-1-IE01-KA220-VET-000257661

#CoHER #ConstructHerFuture #ErasmusPlus #NőkAzÉpítőiparban #Szakképzés #KIA

blocks.heading: Meghívó — CoHER helyi találkozó
2026. augusztus 10. — HU | Mentorokat keresünk a CoHER programhoz
blocks.body:
Van építőipari vagy kapcsolódó műszaki tapasztalatod, amelyet szívesen megosztanál egy pályája elején járó nővel? A Kreatív Ifjúsági Akadémia Magyarország mentorok jelentkezését várja a CoHER mentorprogramba. Nők és férfiak egyaránt lehetnek mentorok. Korábbi mentorálási tapasztalat nem szükséges.

A mentor egy építőipar iránt érdeklődő női szakképzésben tanulót vagy pályakezdő nőt támogat. A beszélgetések során segíthetsz neki megismerni a szakmai lehetőségeket, a munkahelyi helyzeteket és a fejlődéséhez szükséges készségeket. A feladatod a tapasztalataid megosztása, a kérdések meghallgatása és a használható visszajelzés. A mentorált a saját céljairól és következő lépéseiről maga dönt.

Érdekel a mentorálás? Írj az info@becya.org címre, és néhány mondatban mutasd be a szakmai területedet, tapasztalatodat és azt, miért vennél részt.

blocks.heading: 10 August 2026 — EN | Mentors wanted for CoHER
blocks.body:
Do you have experience in construction or a related technical field that you would like to share with a woman starting her career? Kreatív Ifjúsági Akadémia Magyarország invites expressions of interest from CoHER mentors. Women and men can both be mentors. Previous mentoring experience is not required.

A mentor supports a female VET learner interested in construction or an early-career woman in the sector. Conversations can help her understand career routes, workplace situations and useful skills. Your role is to share experience, listen to her questions and offer constructive guidance. The mentee makes her own decisions about her goals and next steps.

Interested in mentoring? Email info@becya.org with a short introduction to your field, experience and reason for taking part.

pages.title: INCLUDE — October 2026: One Year of INCLUDE: Keeping Inclusion at the Centre

blocks.heading: October 2026: One Year of INCLUDE: Keeping Inclusion at the Centre
blocks.body:
October marks one year since the start of INCLUDE. Its programme connects international mobilities, virtual events, policy dialogue, and cooperation between partners in Bulgaria, Türkiye, and Hungary.

For Creative Youth Academy, the project brings attention to an enduring question: how can digital education welcome young people with different abilities, experiences, and learning needs?

STEAM, coding, and artificial intelligence offer many possibilities, but meaningful participation requires attention to accessibility and support. As INCLUDE continues, we remain committed to the idea that young people should have opportunities to learn, contribute, and help shape a more inclusive digital future.

Photo: Partner coordination and project visibility work from the project’s TPM2 archive.

pages.title: INCLUDE — September 2026: INCLUDE Partners Meet for TPM2

blocks.heading: September 2026: INCLUDE Partners Meet for TPM2
blocks.body:
INCLUDE’s second transnational project meeting took place on 26 September 2026, marking another coordination milestone for the partnership.

International projects depend on communication between partners as well as their public activities. Coordination helps maintain a shared direction across different countries, responsibilities, and learning settings.

Creative Youth Academy’s role as the Hungarian partner remains connected to INCLUDE’s central purpose: supporting more inclusive digital and STEAM education. As the project moves through its later stages, accessibility, youth participation, and the continuing value of learning experiences remain important themes for the partnership.

Photo: Partner coordination meeting from the project’s TPM2 archive.

pages.title: INCLUDE — August 2026: Hungary Organises an INCLUDE Virtual Event

blocks.heading: August 2026: Hungary Organises an INCLUDE Virtual Event
blocks.body:
On 15 and 16 August 2026, Creative Youth Academy organised the Hungarian virtual event within INCLUDE.

The event formed part of the project’s combination of physical mobilities and online activities. This international structure supports the partnership’s shared focus on inclusive digital education and opportunities for continued cooperation.

For Creative Youth Academy, accessibility is an ongoing consideration in both physical and virtual learning spaces. Providing different ways to connect can help broaden participation, while clear communication and supportive formats remain essential. The Hungarian event represents another milestone in INCLUDE’s collaboration across Bulgaria, Türkiye, and Hungary.

Photo: INCLUDE Hungarian virtual event, August 2026, from the project’s shared archive.

pages.title: INCLUDE — July 2026: A Month for Digital Inclusion and Youth Policy

blocks.heading: July 2026: A Month for Digital Inclusion and Youth Policy
blocks.body:
July brought a milestone in INCLUDE’s programme: the Bulgarian mobility, focused on AI policy and digital inclusion, took place from 4 to 10 July 2026.

The project’s wider programme also includes Bulgaria’s “Tech for Inclusion: Digital Innovation & AI-Powered Solutions” virtual event and the Digital Inclusion Expo & AI Policy Fair. The Tech for Inclusion announcement placed access, fairness, responsible AI, and young people’s involvement in designing technology at the centre of its approach.

In its report on the policy fair’s first day, the Bulgarian partner described discussions, presentations, practical tasks, and group work covering AI ethics, digital accessibility, personal data protection, and equal access to technology. Participants explored barriers affecting people with disabilities and young people in smaller communities, and began developing proposals for more accessible, people-centred technology.

As the Hungarian partner, Creative Youth Academy supports opportunities for young people’s perspectives to inform discussions about inclusive digital education.

Photo: From the INCLUDE Bulgaria mobility photo archive, July 2026.

pages.title: INCLUDE — June 2026: Why Young People’s Voices Matter in Digital Education

blocks.heading: June 2026: Why Young People’s Voices Matter in Digital Education
blocks.body:
Who gets to shape the future of digital learning? INCLUDE places youth participation alongside its focus on STEAM, coding, and artificial intelligence.

Young people bring valuable perspectives on how technology fits into their lives and where barriers to learning remain. Meaningful participation means creating opportunities for them to express those perspectives and influence the discussion.

For Creative Youth Academy, digital inclusion involves both access to learning and opportunities to contribute. Supporting young people to ask questions, propose ideas, and consider different viewpoints is central to the project’s educational purpose.

Photo: Official INCLUDE project logo from the project’s Graphic Designs archive.

pages.title: INCLUDE — May 2026: INCLUDE’s AI and Digital Inclusion Mobility in Türkiye

blocks.heading: May 2026: INCLUDE’s AI and Digital Inclusion Mobility in Türkiye
blocks.body:
From 17 to 23 May 2026, INCLUDE’s international mobility programme continued in Balıkesir, Türkiye, with the AI and Digital Inclusion Bootcamp. The organisers’ invitation scheduled the core bootcamp programme for 18–22 May, within this mobility period.

The organising team provided the ConnectMinds platform as a central place for mobility information, updates, and coordination. Their announcement explained that participants received accommodation information and platform instructions directly, while coordinators had a separate registration process.

The bootcamp’s focus connects artificial intelligence with a central project question: how can digital learning become more accessible to young people with diverse learning needs?

Creative Youth Academy is the Hungarian partner in this collaboration with organisations from Türkiye and Bulgaria. Through INCLUDE, we support digital education that brings technical learning together with creativity, critical thinking, and inclusion.

Photo: Participants working with digital tools, from the INCLUDE Türkiye mobility’s Day 4 photo archive.

pages.title: INCLUDE — April 2026: From Online Exchange to Digital Solutions

blocks.heading: April 2026: From Online Exchange to Digital Solutions
blocks.body:
April brought an INCLUDE virtual event organised by the Turkish partner on 26 April, followed by the Digital Solutions Hackathon on 27–28 April 2026.

The hackathon’s challenge brief asked teams from Türkiye, Bulgaria, and Hungary to create an AI-powered digital cultural map. The maps were designed to present each country’s geography, heritage, language, art, food, music, and young people’s perspectives through digital storytelling.

The programme introduced ChatGPT for research and writing, Gemini for visual creation, and Gamma for building digital presentations. Its two-evening format combined introductory training, team development time, and presentations to an international jury. The organisers invited at least two teams per country, with up to five young people in each team.

For Creative Youth Academy, this connects STEAM learning with creativity, intercultural exchange, and opportunities for young people to contribute their own ideas.

Photo: Digital Solutions Hackathon, April 2026: a digital cultural map presentation, from the project’s shared archive.

pages.title: INCLUDE — March 2026: Connecting Online Through INCLUDE

blocks.heading: March 2026: Connecting Online Through INCLUDE
blocks.body:
On 30 March 2026, the Turkish partner organised an INCLUDE virtual event, extending the project’s activities into an online setting.

Virtual learning is an important part of INCLUDE’s approach to connecting young people and educators across Bulgaria, Türkiye, and Hungary. It offers another setting for exploring digital education and maintaining international connections between physical mobilities.

For Creative Youth Academy, meaningful online participation depends on more than access to a screen. Clear communication, understandable materials, and opportunities to contribute are also essential. These principles support the project’s wider aim of making digital learning more accessible to people with different needs.

Photo: INCLUDE Digital STEAM Lab virtual event, March 2026, from the project’s shared archive.

pages.title: INCLUDE — February 2026: Looking Beyond a Mobility Week

blocks.heading: February 2026: Looking Beyond a Mobility Week
blocks.body:
Following January’s Hungarian mobility, February’s INCLUDE spotlight is on the value of reflection in international learning.

A mobility can offer more than an introduction to new subjects. It can encourage young people to think about how they work with others, approach unfamiliar challenges, and communicate their ideas.

Creative Youth Academy supports an approach that recognises these broader dimensions of learning. Reflecting on an experience can help participants identify what interested them, where they need further support, and what they would like to explore next. For INCLUDE, accessibility and youth participation remain relevant throughout that learning journey.

Photo: INCLUDE Hungarian mobility, January 2026, from the project’s shared photo archive.

pages.title: INCLUDE — January 2026: Hungary Hosts the INCLUDE STEAM Bootcamp

blocks.heading: January 2026: Hungary Hosts the INCLUDE STEAM Bootcamp
blocks.body:
January marked the Hungarian mobility of INCLUDE, held from 25 to 31 January 2026. A preparatory meeting on 16 January preceded the mobility.

As the Hungarian partner, Creative Youth Academy welcomed this milestone in the project’s international programme. The STEAM Bootcamp connects the project’s focus on creativity, digital learning, and artificial intelligence with opportunities for cooperation across borders.

The purpose of this learning approach is to make technology more approachable and relevant to young people with different backgrounds and learning needs. Bringing the partnership together in Hungary also creates space for intercultural exchange around a shared commitment to inclusive education.

Photo: INCLUDE STEAM Bootcamp in Hungary, January 2026, from the project’s shared photo archive.

pages.title: INCLUDE — December 2025: Connecting Creativity, STEAM, and Artificial Intelligence

blocks.heading: December 2025: Connecting Creativity, STEAM, and Artificial Intelligence
blocks.body:
INCLUDE brings creativity into the conversation about digital education. Coding and artificial intelligence offer opportunities to explore ideas, solve problems, and develop new ways of learning.

The project’s planned learning themes include STEAM foundations, AI awareness, and digital inclusion. Together, they encourage an approach in which technical knowledge grows alongside teamwork, critical thinking, and social awareness.

At Creative Youth Academy, we believe young people should be encouraged to explore both the possibilities and limitations of technology. Accessible digital education should help learners make informed choices and develop the confidence to contribute their own ideas.

Photo: Official INCLUDE project artwork from the project’s Graphic Designs archive.

pages.title: INCLUDE — November 2025: Different Learning Needs, Equal Opportunities

blocks.heading: November 2025: Different Learning Needs, Equal Opportunities
blocks.body:
What makes digital learning accessible? Through INCLUDE, Creative Youth Academy highlights the importance of recognising that young people learn in different ways.

Clear instructions, flexible activities, accessible materials, and supportive learning environments can help more young people participate in STEAM — science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics. The project’s approach connects these subjects with creativity and everyday problem-solving.

Our priority as the Hungarian partner is to support opportunities where young people can contribute their ideas, ask questions, and explore technology at a pace that works for them. Inclusion starts with listening and making space for different perspectives.

Photo: Official INCLUDE promotional artwork from the project’s Graphic Designs archive.

pages.title: INCLUDE — October 2025: Making Digital Learning More Inclusive

blocks.heading: October 2025: Introducing INCLUDE: Making Digital Learning More Inclusive
blocks.body:
Creative Youth Academy is the Hungarian partner in INCLUDE — Innovative Coding and Learning for Unique Development in Education. This Erasmus+ youth participation project connects organisations in Bulgaria, Türkiye, and Hungary around a shared goal: making digital and STEAM learning more accessible to young people with diverse learning needs.

The project’s first partner meeting took place on 5 October 2025. INCLUDE brings together digital literacy, coding, artificial intelligence, and youth participation. For Creative Youth Academy, its central message is clear: young people should have opportunities to help shape the learning experiences and technologies that affect their lives.

Photo: INCLUDE kick-off meeting, 5 October 2025, from the project’s shared archive.

blocks.heading: About the Event
blocks.body: We are pleased to share the successful implementation of a local event under the Visegrad Project ID: 22510078, coordinated by Mission: Reconnect, z.s. & Creative Youth Academy in Budapest, Hungary, on the 26th of January 2026.

blocks.heading: What We Did
blocks.body:
As part of our ongoing efforts to foster sustainable communities, a dedicated workshop was organized to enhance environmental and ecological awareness among young people. The session focused on building knowledge, encouraging dialogue, and inspiring participants to take an active role in addressing environmental challenges.

Through interactive discussions and practical insights, participants were empowered to engage in community-driven initiatives, particularly in the area of community gardening as a tool for sustainability, cooperation, and local resilience.
